answer: Oppo appears to be positioning the Watch X3 as a premium, tough-built smartwatch rather than chasing the ultra-thin trend that others are leaning into right now. A titanium alloy bezel and sapphire crystal display protection are both on the list, which would put the Watch X3 in premium territory. Weight is expected to come in around 68 grams with color options spanning black, silver, titanium, and orange. The design sticks with the round form factor used on the Watch X2 and there's a rotating crown alongside a second side button for hardware navigation. That combination of touch and physical controls has become a signature of the Watch X line. On the display side, a 1.5-inch LTPO AMOLED panel is. Its peak brightness is at around 2,200 nits. Internally, the Watch X3 is to carry a dual-chip setup, which Oppo has used before to balance performance with power efficiency. The idea is that a low-power co-processor handles background tasks and standby, keeping the main chip free for heavier lifting. RAM and storage are expected to land at 2 gigabytes and 32 gigabytes respectively. The battery capacity is at 632 milliamp hours, which is on the larger end for a Wear OS device. The Watch X2 already stood out for its endurance, so a bigger cell in the X3 would only strengthen that reputation. Software is Wear OS 6, based on Android 16, bringing Google Maps, Wallet, and Play Store access along with it. Connectivity should cover LTE with eSIM, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and NFC for payments. Health features are expected to include heart rate, sleep tracking, GPS, and a range of sports modes with ECG. The Watch X3 looks more like an evolution of the Watch X2 than a fresh start. Oppo seems to be taking what already worked and turning up the dial in a few specific areas. For now, the March 17th date is the one to watch.

answer: The roar of the machines of the Industrial Revolution signaled momentous changes. The steam-driven machines of the Victorian era transformed the world. Automation created entirely new industries that allowed factories to produce goods on an unimaginable scale. Goods were traded around the world, and in return, exotic goods from the far corners of the globe were imported. If you were part of the middle class, it was a time of plenty and a cornucopia of goods from all over the world could be purchased at one of the latest innovations, the department store. In the glittering surrounding of Harrod's, can be found practically anything from almost anywhere in the world. Ivory goods from the Orient, ebony from darkest Africa, sandwich glass from Massachusetts, coffee from Brazil, porcelain from the Orient. Of all the products available to the well-to-do in the Victorian age, one of the most indispensable was whale oil. Its superior lubricating qualities made whale oil the ideal product to keep industrial steam engines operating. But whale oil was also used on the domestic front. Whale oil lamps lit up the homes of the wealthy and fashionable. It provided a brighter light than other animal fats available and produced far less smoke. Whale oil was extensively used in toiletries, cosmetics, and soaps. While whale oil was highly prized, whale bone too was a much sought-after product. In many ways, whale bone was the plastic of its day. It was strong and flexible and could be put to numerous uses. Whalebone was used to make buggy whips, as well as the springs on which the carriages rode. It was used to make brushes, combs, the ribs for parasols and umbrellas, and fishing rods. But it was in women's fashion that whalebone made the greatest impression. To complete the ensemble, voluminous skirts supported by hoops of whalebone were all the rage in fashionable society. Whalebone and oil were luxury products, but the fashions and technology of the day meant there was a ready market willing to pay a premium for them.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Flat-headed cats have been successfully detected and filmed in southern Thailand for the first time in almost 30 years. One of the world's rarest cats, it was last documented here back in 1995, leading some to believe it was possibly extinct. Conservationists, however, thought otherwise. We had heard reports for many years and were confident that the species was still present. Rettapan Padinarinsen, conservation program manager for Panthera Thailand, told IFL Science. What was needed was the right study design to confirm it. The largest ever survey of the species began in 2024, using camera traps from Thailand's Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, and Panthera Thailand, a global wildcat conservation organization. 13 detections were made in 2024, and a further 16 detections were made in 2025. Most exciting of all, the observations included a female flat-headed cat with her cub. Flat-headed cats are the smallest in Southeast Asia. They weigh half that of a typical domestic cat and have a distinctive flattened forehead and elongated skull. They are small, nocturnal and prefer to occupy dense terrain, making searching for them in the wild that much harder. Even catching them on camera traps can be difficult. But using lessons learned from studying fishing cats, Panthera were able to identify the best sites for camera placement, leading to the successful detection and photographic evidence of the flat-headed cat. It's estimated there are 2,500 flat-headed cats globally, and they're classed as endangered by the IUCN, but in Thailand, it was considered possibly extinct. A new Panthera-led IUCN assessment is now expected in 2026.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: A controversial new budget draft was withdrawn on Thursday morning after thousands of protesters took to the streets of Sofia to oppose it the night before. The government had proposed to increase social security contributions and double dividend taxes in an ambitious new budget, which would have set a new spending record at around 46% of GDP, as well as dramatically increased public debt. Wednesday evening's rally was organized by the opposition coalition and is estimated to have drawn around 20,000 people. Protesters gathered outside the National Assembly building, where lawmakers convened to examine the proposed budget. They formed a massive human chain around the parliament building in an effort to block all exits and prevent MPs from leaving the premises. Police say the protests, which were declared as peaceful, quickly escalated and turned violent, announcing that three police officers were injured. Authorities say some protesters threw firecrackers and glass bottles at deployed officers and attempted to overturn a police van. The protest came ahead of a final parliamentary vote to gain approval and just a few weeks before the Balkan nation is set to enter the Eurozone.

What happened to us over the past 15 years, did not only happen to us, it also happened to all of you in Europe. It all started when those in power single out usually the most vulnerable groups in society and try to portray them as the enemy within. That should be the first sign that you need to watch for. I want to live in a country where you can have frank, decent conversations, even disagreements without taking a huge risk. Now is the time to actually act and to show that destroying democracy and undermining human rights have clear consequences in the European Union.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: I'm Adriana Tuzu. I used to work as a criminal judge for 24 years and I resigned in last December. Judicial independence is not an easy thing to digest. I would say that there are still independent judges in Hungary, but the whole system is not independent anymore. Tens of thousands of Hungarians protested long into the night against the government's rewriting of the constitution. There are two main actors who are defining the position of judiciary. These are elected in order to influence the decisions of the Supreme Court in favor of the government. Nowadays, they can also overrule the decisions of the Court of the European Union. Now, Hungary is embroiled in a legal battle with the European Union. First of all, we should define what is European Union, Brussels. They should be our servant. If you want to be successful as a judge, you have to be loyal, otherwise you wouldn't get forward. And on the other hand, if you are not, if you speak up, you have to face difficulties. I quit judiciary after 28 years working at the same court, among the same people, and I missed this the most. It was a really hard decision to make. I was born to be a judge, and I really identified as one. Uh, as as a in my in my personal life, the fact that I had to leave, I still dream about it. A lot. Being a judge. I got a quite a huge media coverage after my resignation. Nowadays I'm trying to do my best to help from the outside. I can speak up and I can tell our stories and that can make people understand what the problem is. History taught us that there is always a way out of everything. There have to be certain values that cannot be negotiated. And the European Union has the power to make all the member states appreciate those values.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: 2025 is packed with incredible humanoid robots. But this viral clip from Iran's Kish Invex tech exhibition proves that not everything that looks robotic is actually advanced. The video starts off looking legit, bright expo lights, a cybersecurity booth, and two humanoid robots, dressed in white suits covered with binary code. They wave, pose, greet visitors, and move in stiff, mechanical ways, just convincing enough to make people wonder if they're looking at a new AI demo. But something feels off. The robots blink too much. Their movements are more cosplay than engineering. And those giant purple sunglasses, a bit too stylish for a supposed next-gen android. Still, the crowd plays along. People ask questions, shake hands, take photos. The performers stay in character, talking in monotone voices. Hello, how are you? Can you move like us? What kind of work can we do for you? And then, the moment that broke the internet. The male robot turns revealing a white plastic shopping bag hanging from his shoulder. A normal, everyday bag on an advanced humanoid machine. Instant laughter. Someone shouts, I thought it was a robot. There's a man inside. And just like that, the illusion collapses. It wasn't a breakthrough robot. It wasn't a secret prototype. It was just two dedicated performers promoting a booth, until one simple prop exposed everything. And the funniest part? This clip spread faster than many real robotics announcements. Because in a world filled with hype, sometimes the internet just loves a good not-a-robot moment. This is Robo Frontier, where we cover the real breakthroughs and the hilarious ones too.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The Global South's mineral wealth, a game changer for economic growth, but at what cost? The G20's 2025 Summit in Johannesburg, South Africa has ignited a crucial conversation about the role of critical minerals in shaping our future. But here's where it gets controversial. Can these resources truly drive inclusive growth and resilience, or will they perpetuate existing inequalities? In a bold move, the G20 has unveiled its critical minerals framework, aiming to transform these essential resources into catalysts for sustainable development. The plan? To empower mineral rich nations, particularly in the Global South, to move beyond simply exporting raw materials. And this is the part most people miss. The framework seeks to address the systemic challenges these countries face, from underinvestment and limited technology to socio-economic and environmental hurdles. As the world undergoes rapid economic transformations, think sustainable energy transitions, digitalization, and industrial innovation, the demand for critical minerals is skyrocketing. However, the G20 declaration highlights a stark reality. Many producer countries, especially developing nations, are struggling to capitalize on this opportunity. The framework offers a voluntary, non-binding road map to foster sustainable, transparent, and resilient mineral value chains. This includes boosting investment in exploration, promoting local processing, beneficiation, and strengthening governance for responsible mining practices. Here's the catch. While the framework promises to preserve the sovereign rights of mineral rich countries, it also raises questions about equitable benefit sharing and environmental stewardship. Will local communities truly reap the rewards or will multinational corporations dominate the landscape. The G20 encourages collaboration among governments, private sectors, investors, and local communities, but how will this play out in practice? Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of international cooperation in addressing global challenges from climate change to food systems. India's commitment to a human-centric, sustainable, and inclusive future aligns with the G20's vision. But as the summit concludes, one question lingers, can critical minerals truly become a force for broad-based development, or will they remain a source of raw material exports leaving the global south behind? What's your take? Do you believe the G20's critical minerals framework can deliver on its promises, or are there inherent flaws in the approach? Share your thoughts in the comments. Let's spark a conversation that could shape the future of global resource management.

Today, we're diving into the story of the largest polar bear ever recorded, a true giant that shattered records and left scientists stunned. Let's rewind to 1960 in the icy region of Kotzebue Sound, Alaska. A group of hunters came across a truly enormous male polar bear and what they found would go down in history. This bear wasn't just large, it was colossal. When officially measured, the bear stood 11 ft 1 in 3.4 m tall when upright and weighed an unbelievable 2,209 lb. That's over 1 ton of arctic muscle and fur. To put that in perspective, that's heavier than a Toyota Corolla and taller than a basketball hoop when standing on its hind legs. Most adult male polar bears weigh between 900 and 1,500 lbs. So this monster of the North was far beyond the normal range. Scientists estimate it was likely in its prime and had access to an exceptional hunting territory, probably feeding on plenty of seals and possibly even beluga carcasses. Its skull alone was record-breaking, measuring 16.25 inches long and 11.75 inches wide, making it one of the largest carnivore skulls ever documented. The bear was later taxidermied and displayed. It serves as a powerful reminder of the extremes nature can produce and of the polar bear's status as one of Earth's ultimate apex predators. But here's the twist, as climate change continues to shrink arctic ice and reduce hunting grounds, polar bears are getting smaller on average. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Most worlds end once, but this one has died and returned more times than anyone can count. Every time the snow melts, the servers close, and then somehow someone brings it all back. When we return, we aren't just logging in. We're re-entering a piece of ourselves that we thought we'd outgrown. When we built these penguins, we didn't just pick colors or clothes. We built versions of who we hoped to be. The confident one in red, the quiet one in blue, the dreamer, the explorer, the one who finally fit in. We were shaping identity before we even knew the word for it. There is a psychological theory called the Proteus effect. It says when you change your avatar, your behavior changes with it. Maybe that's why the shy kids led the conga lines here. Maybe that's why the lonely ones hosted parties every night. It was safer to be bold when you were just made of pixels. In here, we could be someone else. And sometimes, that's the truest version of who we are. Every snowball was a conversation, every emote was a way of saying I see you in a language that nobody taught us. Connection didn't need a voice chat, just timing, intention, a small gesture across the screen. We were learning empathy without knowing its name. The dojo was the only place where stillness felt like progress. No coins, no leaderboards, just patience. For once, the goal wasn't just to win, it was to understand a rhythm and yourself. It's 2025, and somehow we are here again. Different people, same avatars. The penguins grew up, but they returned anyway. Maybe because this world never judged us for who we were or who we were trying to become. Every home we built here was a fragment of comfort. We arranged these rooms like we arranged our hearts, cluttered, colorful, and desperately personal. There's something tender about rebuilding a world no one asked you to bring back. Club Penguin Zero isn't about nostalgia. It's about proof that versions of ourselves we once loved still exist somewhere, waiting under the snow. We return to remember. We stay to rebuild. I've been delayed but I will be there around that time.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Curious commuters recently noticed a massive vault-like door near Exit 5 of Taipei Metro's Nanjing Fushing Station, sparking online speculation about its purpose. Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation clarified that the heavy, sealed structure is a flood barrier system, a vital defense mechanism designed after the devastating floods caused by Typhoon Nari in 2001. During that storm, floodwaters inundated the Blue Bannan Line and even swamped Taipei Main Station, reaching depths of up to 2.3 m. The disaster led Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation to design and install multiple waterproof systems across the network. If flooding threatens, this watertight door, 30 cm thick, can be closed to prevent water from entering the platform level, said CTS reporter Chang Hsiaoyun, while demonstrating the mechanism on site. According to Huang Yi Chao, a section chief from the Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit systems, the doors were introduced after engineers realized that flooding could easily overwhelm stations entrances. We decided to place basic waterproofing at the entrances and add full seal floodgates at station interfaces, he explained. The Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation uses several types of flood barriers, including swinging, vertical, and sliding models, to block water from penetrating underground areas. Although forecasts predict less rain from this week's Typhoon Fung Wong than from Nari, with expected totals around 300 mm over 2 days, city officials said the metro system remains on high alert to ensure uninterrupted service. Filip Stawski for ICRT News.

question: Describe the audio content in detail.
answer:
This video provides an educational overview of the AIDAAS model, a structured framework for effective communication. The presenter guides the listener through each of the five stages: Attention (capturing your audience's focus), Interest (sparking curiosity with relevant information), Desire (creating a want for your offering), Action (prompting a specific next step with a clear call to action), and Satisfaction (ensuring long-term happiness and building relationships). The tutorial offers practical tips for each phase, encourages practice through exercises, and concludes by prompting reflection on the ethical application of this powerful communication tool.

Welcome. Today we delve into the AIDAAS model, a powerful tool to elevate your communication. The AIDAAS model is a structured approach that guides your audience through the journey of communication. Are you ready to learn the secrets of successful communication? Let's get started.

Attention is the first crucial step. You need to capture your audience's attention immediately. In a world of information overload, a structured approach is key to making your message stand out. Use powerful headlines, striking images, and focus on the benefit for your audience to grab attention.

Once you have attention, you must spark interest. This is where you engage your audience further. Reveal the hook by making your message relevant to your audience. This is about you. Engage interest with facts, relatable stories, and highlight how your product or idea solves their problem.

Now, transform interest into desire. Your audience should want what you're offering. Your goal is to form the 'I want it' response. Make them feel a strong desire for your offering. Connect emotionally, visualize the outcome, show social proof, and use restrictions to drive desire.

The action stage is about getting your audience to take the desired next step. Provide a clear call to action (CTA). Tell them exactly what you want them to do. Make taking action as simple as possible. Remove any obstacles that might stop them.

Satisfaction is about ensuring your audience is happy. After the action is taken, turn a client into a fan by building long-term relationships. Go beyond the sale to ensure their satisfaction. Provide excellent support, service, and ensure you fulfill your promise to solidify satisfaction.

Let's walk through an example of AIDAAS in action with a new digital marketing course. We'll illustrate how to apply each stage of the AIDAAS model to advertise a new digital marketing course.

Now it's your turn to practice. Let's create your own AIDAAS strategy. Analyze a familiar ad using AIDAAS. Then, try to create a short message using the AIDAAS model.

Let's take a moment to reflect and consider the ethical implications of using AIDAAS. Consider when the AIDAAS model might not be sufficient and how does ethics affect its application.

It's time to put what you've learned into practice. Your mini-step is to apply the AIDAAS model to one message today. See what results you can achieve.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: How did journalists cover the Berlin Wall's construction? Imagine waking up to a city suddenly divided overnight. That's exactly what happened on August 13, 1961, when the Berlin Wall began to rise. Journalists were quick to report this startling change, capturing the shock and confusion felt by Berliners. News outlets described how barbed wire and barricades appeared suddenly, cutting East Berlin off from West Berlin. Reporters used vivid words like barbed wire, steel barriers, and military presence to paint a picture of the tense scene. Radio stations, especially from the American sector, played a vital role. Stations like Radio in the American Sector provided live updates, warning people about the new restrictions and urging caution. Journalists on the ground described soldiers reinforcing the wall with steel barriers and East German troops patrolling the border. Newspapers in the West published eyewitness accounts, emphasizing how families were separated and freedoms restricted. They highlighted the speed of construction and the human toll of this sudden division. West Berlin's leaders, including the mayor, expressed outrage and called for support from Western allies. These statements were widely covered, showing the political tension. The East German government initially denied plans to build a wall, with leaders like Walter Ulbricht claiming there was no intention to do so. As the wall went up, journalists reported on this contradiction, illustrating the propaganda battles happening alongside the physical construction. International coverage also focused on the broader Cold War tensions. Reports described US troop movements and the famous tank confrontation at Checkpoint Charlie later that year. Journalists framed the wall as a symbol of communist oppression and the deep ideological divide between East and West. During the 1960s, coverage was full of urgency and emotion. Reporters told stories of fear, hope, and resilience of Berliners living through one of the Cold War's most defining moments. They combined eyewitness accounts with political analysis, capturing the era's style of reporting. This coverage helped the world understand the significance of the Berlin Wall's construction and its impact on global politics.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: There are many ways to build a quantum computer. Each uses qubits, quantum bits, as its core building block. But no matter the method, all qubits, whether superconducting qubits, trapped ions, neutral atoms or photons, share the same challenge. They're fragile and extremely sensitive to noise. Today's qubits remain stable for only a few hundred operations, but solving meaningful problems requires trillions of operations. The answer is quantum error correction. Measuring disturbs a qubit, which destroys the information inside it. The trick is to add extra qubits, entangled, so that measuring them gives us enough information to calculate where errors occurred without damaging the qubits we care about. It's brilliant, but needs beyond state-of-the-art conventional compute. That's why we built NVQLink, a new interconnect architecture that directly connects quantum processors with Nvidia GPUs. Quantum error correction requires reading out information from qubits, calculating where errors occur, and sending data back to correct them. NVQLink is capable of moving terabytes of data to and from quantum hardware, the thousands of times every second needed for quantum error correction. At its heart is CUDA-Q, our open platform for quantum GPU computing. Using NVQLink and CUDA-Q, researchers will be able to do more than just error correction. They will also be able to orchestrate quantum devices and AI supercomputers to run quantum GPU applications. Quantum computing won't replace classical systems. They will work together, fused into one accelerated quantum supercomputing platform.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: I have with me right now the TCL NXT Paper 14 and the TCL NXT Paper 11 Plus. and over the past couple of months, I have been testing out these two tablets. So, I just wanted to give you guys my honest thoughts on them, see how they stack up against each other. And overall, give you guys just a few things to consider before you settle on one of the two. The first and most obvious difference between the two is obviously going to be the screen size. The 11 Plus is lighter, faster, and more portable. It's got an 11 and a half inch 2.2K display and runs on NXT Paper 4.0 technology. Not only that, but it also has a 120 Hz refresh rate, and that refresh rate is going to be super important, especially for someone that values a lot smoother and more seamless browsing experience. When you compare the two, the 11 Plus is smoother for navigation, animations, and stylus interactions, while the 14 is geared more towards reading, writing, and large format use. The 11 Plus comes with a stylus, supports pressure assist, and unlike the Paper 14, it comes with a few different AI features like text assist and writing assist. You're also getting an 8 GB RAM and 8 GB of virtual memory storage, as well as 256 GB of regular storage, which is on par with the Paper 14. One key difference with the 11 Plus is that it's getting a faster MediaTek G100 chip, all packed into a slim and lightweight body just under 500 grams. The battery sizes on the two tablets will differ slightly as well. The 11 Plus comes with an 8,000 mAh hour battery while the 14 comes with a 10,000 mAh hour battery. Honestly, although the 11 Plus did come with a smaller battery, I found that the difference in battery life with just normal practical use was pretty negligible. I typically got around two days of moderate use out of both tablets and well over a week of standby time. Now, if you're someone that values screen real estate a lot more, the NXT Paper 14 definitely delivers. This tablet has a huge 14.3-inch display, also comes with a 2.4K resolution. However, it only has a 60 Hz refresh rate. In terms of software, it's running NXT Paper 3.0, which focuses more on a paper-like and anti-glare look, and it's definitely perfect for sketching or reading. You still get the stylus with 4,096 pressure levels, plus a flip case and multi-window multitasking. Overall, I thought there was a lot more of a heavier emphasis on productivity and multitasking with the Paper 14 opposed to the 11 Plus. And that probably had to do with the bigger screen and the ability to switch through different tabs fairly easily. The 11 Plus was definitely meant to be a lot more portable and an easier alternative for students that didn't want to take around a bulky laptop to class. The key takeaways that I got from this experience is that the 11 Plus is more balanced for hybrid use. It offers a high refresh rate, a more advanced display generation, lighter weight, AI features, and a comfortable size for one-hand or mixed usage. On the other hand, the 14 is better suited if your priority is to have a larger canvas. It's really good for reading long documents, viewing diagrams, or large pages, multitasking, or using it more like an actual tablet or digital notebook. You'll ultimately be trading off portability and smoothness for a more immersive experience. All in all, I do think both tablets do have their pros and cons, and ultimately, it kind of just boils down to how you want to use it and how you envision it in your day-to-day life. All things considered, I definitely still recommend both tablets as really strong contenders against the competition.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The quiet visitors. Not every comet is a headline grabber. Some slip through the solar system as faint smudges, their passage noted only by dedicated observers. Among the seven visitors of 2025, two fall into this quiet category. C 2022 E3 or Panstars, and the periodic comet, 240p NEET. C 2022 E3 reaches its perihelion on July 31st at a chilly distance of 3.82 astronomical units, or about 571 million kilometers from the sun. At that range, it's not expected to brighten beyond a modest magnitude 10, visible only in medium-sized telescopes. Then there's 240p NEET, which was discovered in 2002 and returns every 7.6 years. It makes its pass on December 19th at a distance of 2.12 astronomical units, or 317 million kilometers. Its performance will likely be even dimmer, a low key encore for those tracking its well-documented path. For both of these objects, the primary audience will be astronomers contributing data to the minor Planet Center, where every verified observation helps refine orbital calculations. Even these faint comets provide crucial data on things like nucleus rotation and the slow development of their comas. They are the workhorses of cometary science, providing a baseline of normal activity against which the brighter comets can be compared.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Imagine a city already reeking of plague, piled high with timber houses, and stuffed with gunpowder. Then picture one careless spark. That was London, 1666. A tinderbox waiting to explode. It all began in a tiny bakery on Pudding Lane. A spark caught, the flame spread, and within hours, London was an inferno. Roofs collapsed, fireballs lept across streets, and terrified families clawed through smoke trying to escape. The city's wooden homes burned like matchsticks, while the wind turned alleys into fire tunnels. People fled, carrying whatever they could, some clutching furniture, others dragging half-burnt livestock. Most with nothing but ash on their skin. The fire raged for four days. St. Paul's Cathedral, that proud symbol of London, crumbled in the flames. Warehouses full of oil, tar, and brandy exploded into firestorms. By the end, over 13,000 houses and 87 churches were reduced to charred rubble. And while the city burned, rumors spread like sparks. Foreigners were blamed, Catholics were accused of sabotage, innocents were lynched in the streets by mobs who thought the fire was a plot. But here's the real kicker. London wasn't just burning, it was already crawling with plague. The fire roared through neighborhoods where corpses still lay rotting in homes. Some whispered the flames were God's punishment, others that it was mercy, burning the pestilence out. In the chaos, law and order collapsed. Looters picked through burning ruins. Rioters murdered anyone they suspected of starting it. The city was a vision of hell where firelight made night look like blood red day. When the smoke finally cleared, 100,000 Londoners were homeless. Families slept in fields under the September rain. The city stank of ash, rot, and despair. Yet somehow, from the wreckage, London began to rebuild. Brick by brick, flameproof this time. The Great Fire didn't just destroy London. It reshaped it. It burned away the medieval heart of the city, replacing it with something new. But for those who watched their world turn to cinders, it was the apocalypse.

Boston's Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority provides detailed maps of bus routes and the subway system, especially the red line that stops at Harvard Square. These transit maps help you plan your trip from Boston to Harvard easily. If you want a physical keepsake, printed maps of Harvard's main campus and Harvard Square are available for purchase online or at local stores. These maps often show the Charles River, Harvard Yard and surrounding streets, giving you a broader view of the area. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Can I take a self-guided tour of Harvard University? Imagine walking through one of the most famous college campuses in the world, all at your own pace. If that sounds exciting, you might wonder if you can explore Harvard University on your own. The good news is yes, you can take a self-guided tour of Harvard. The campus and the nearby Cambridge area are very welcoming to visitors who want to see the sights without a group. You can plan your own route to visit key spots like Harvard Yard, the historic center of the university, and the John Harvard statue, which is a popular photo spot. You can also check out Widener Library, a stunning building filled with millions of books, and Memorial Hall, a grand structure built to honor Harvard students who served in wars. Harvard Square, the lively neighborhood around the campus, is full of shops, cafes, and street performers, making it a fun place to explore on your own. To make your self-guided tour easier, Harvard offers downloadable maps and GPS-enabled audio guides. These guides give you background stories and facts about each landmark, so you learn as you walk. Harvard University is located in Cambridge, just across the Charles River from Boston, so it's easy to reach by public transit. The best way to start your tour is by taking the Red Line subway, called the T, to the Harvard Square station. Once there, you can begin your walk at popular spots like Out of Town Newsstand or the Harvard Square MBTA station. The typical self-guided tour covers about 1.4 miles and takes around 2 hours. This gives you plenty of time to see everything without rushing. If you want to spend more time at certain sites, you can easily do so. While self-guided tours do not include a live guide, the maps and audio guides provide enough information to make your visit interesting and educational. Harvard also offers guided tours led by students, which give more detailed stories and insights. But if you prefer exploring on your own, the self-guided option is a flexible and popular choice. From the perspective of the city of Boston, Harvard is a nearby cultural and educational landmark. It's a quick trip across the river, making it perfect for residents and visitors who want to experience a historic university on their own schedule. So, yes, you absolutely can take a self-guided tour of Harvard University and enjoy discovering its history and beauty at your own pace.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Let's talk about a man who looks at our world and thinks, not enough. I'm talking about Elon Musk. As of today, August 29th, 2025, he is the wealthiest person on our planet with a fortune built on electric cars, solar panels, and of course, rockets. But Musk isn't just collecting billions of dollars to build bigger houses or own more companies. He has a much grander, some would say much stranger goal. He wants to die on Mars. Not from a crash landing, mind you, but of old age as a resident of a new human civilization on the red planet. This isn't just a casual wish. It is the central driving force behind his life's work and the ultimate destination for his vast fortune. Why Mars? Why pour hundreds of billions of dollars into a project that many see as pure science fiction? For Musk, the answer is simple and profound. Survival. He views humanity as living in a single fragile basket. Earth is that basket. A catastrophic event, a massive asteroid impact, a super volcano, or even a self-inflicted disaster like a global war, could wipe us out completely. To ensure the long-term survival of human consciousness and our species, he argues, we must become multi-planetary. It's a form of cosmic life insurance. He has even pointed to the eventual expansion of our own sun, which will one day make Earth uninhabitable, framing this mission with an almost biblical sense of urgency. This motivation goes beyond just a backup plan. There's a philosophical and perhaps even a political layer to his ambition. For years, Musk presented Mars as a new frontier, a blank slate where humanity could start over, free from the old problems of Earth. It was a vision of a libertarian paradise among the stars. However, recent reports, particularly from his old colleague, Peter Thiel, suggest a shift in his thinking. The fear that a woke AI or a sprawling Earth-based government could simply follow humanity to Mars, has apparently tempered his view of the red planet as a political escape hatch, complicating his once clear-cut futuristic narrative. This grand vision isn't just talk. Musk has dedicated his wealth, estimated at over 335 billion dollars earlier this year, to making this happen. He has repeatedly stated that the entire purpose of accumulating his fortune is to fund the colonization of Mars. This makes him a unique figure in the history of wealth. While other billionaires have focused on philanthropy here on Earth, Musk's philanthropic project is on a planetary scale. He is the modern equivalent of a Pharaoh building a pyramid, not as a tomb, but as a launch pad to a new world. His companies, SpaceX and Tesla, are the tools he is forging for this monumental task.

answer: About a quarter acre of heavy brush burned uphill near the 2,100 block of North Sunset Plaza Drive, threatening several homes above the fire. The Los Angeles Fire Department dispatched roughly 80 personnel, supported by helicopters and hand crews. Aerial water drops significantly slowed the blaze's advance toward residences. Initial reports indicated a vehicle fire that spread into medium heavy brush toward a hillside home. Mutual aid air and ground units from LA County Fire also responded. By evening, crews had extinguished all active flames and stopped the fire's forward progress. Helicopters continued water drops between homes to cool hotspots, while hand crews worked uphill on steep terrain aiming for full containment. Ground crews prioritized structure defense for the at-risk houses. Authorities issued shelter in place orders for Genesis zones LFDO817, LFDO819 and LFDO911. No civilian injuries were reported. Separately that morning, a two-story house on the 10,300 block of North Christine Place in Chatsworth caught fire after flames were observed on the first floor and spreading toward the rear. About 37 firefighters initiated an immediate offensive. The blaze was reported knocked down by 11:39 a.m. with around 53 personnel handling suppression, overhaul and scene stabilization. All occupants were evacuated and accounted for. One firefighter suffered a minor burn and was treated at the scene. City departments collaborated on the incident. The Department of Water and Power handled utilities, transportation managed traffic disruptions and building and safety conducted structural assessments. Motorists were urged to seek alternate routes due to congestion. Officials credited rapid multi-agency response, aggressive firefighting and aerial support with preventing greater property loss and injuries. Crews remained on scene working hotspots and containment.

At the IAA Mobility 2025 Munich event, BMW Motorad introduced the Vision CE, an electric scooter concept that is truly different from most. Just imagine, riders won't need to wear helmets or protective jackets anymore. The secret lies in the inherent safety structure at the heart of its design. An idea that BMW actually tried more than 25 years ago.
Its history began in 2000 with the BMW C1, a unique scooter featuring a roof, roll cage, and seatbelt. Although not mass-produced, the C1 has a loyal following who prioritize comfort over the classic scooter style. Two decades later, BMW succeeded with the CE04 and CE02, two electric scooters that proved eco-friendly mobility can still be stylish. Now, Vision CE brings the C1 legacy, but in a modern format with proven electric technology. The most striking feature of the Vision CE is the safety cell. A metal alloy tube frame with custom seats and seatbelts. This system is designed to provide protection like a small car cabin, so helmets are no longer mandatory. This approach could be a solution to two major obstacles for two-wheeled commuters, the hassle of wearing gear and feeling hot in warm weather. From a design perspective, the Vision CE appears long, low, and futuristic. The safety frame is lightweight and open, more like an architectural framework than a cage. The chosen colors are simple yet elegant. Matte white combined with black, with neon red accents that give a modern and technical feel. The exposed aluminum details add a sense of robustness, while the matte seats and fine lettering keep the look minimalist. Another interesting feature is the self-balancing technology, which keeps the scooter upright even when stopped. Where was Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon filmed?
Have you ever wondered where the breathtaking scenes of Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon were captured? This iconic film, directed by Ang Lee, is a beautiful representation of Chinese culture and cinema. It takes us back to early 19th-century imperial China, showcasing stunning landscapes and intricate artistry.
The film was primarily shot in China, utilizing a mix of natural beauty and elaborate sets. One of the most notable locations is the Huangshan region in Anhui province. This area is famous for its dramatic granite peaks and lush pine forests, creating a striking backdrop for many scenes. The unique scenery adds depth to the film, making it visually captivating.
Another key filming site is the Anji Bamboo Forest in Zhejiang province. This serene forest is known for its lush bamboo groves, providing a tranquil environment that perfectly complements the film's more peaceful moments. The beauty of this location truly enhances the film's aesthetic.
Beijing, the capital city of China, also played a role in the filming process. The urban landscape of Beijing contributed to the cultural aspects of the story, showcasing the blend of tradition and modernity in Chinese life.
Chengde, located in Hebei province, was another filming location. This city offers a mix of historical and natural settings, which helped to create the film's rich visual narrative. The combination of these diverse locations allowed the filmmakers to capture the essence of Chinese culture.
Additionally, Hengdian World Studios in Zhejiang province was utilized for creating elaborate sets. As the largest film studio in the world, it provided the facilities needed to recreate traditional Chinese architecture and settings. This studio played a vital role in bringing the film's story to life.
Together, these locations contributed to the film's success, highlighting China's rich cultural heritage and stunning natural beauty. Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon is not just a film. answer:
What birds can you see in the Masai Mara?
Have you ever wondered what birds you might encounter in the stunning Masai Mara? This incredible region in Kenya is a paradise for bird lovers, boasting over 580 recorded species. The variety of habitats here, from open savanna to wetlands, supports an amazing range of birds. Let's start with the impressive birds of prey. The Masai Mara is home to many eagle species. You might spot the Tawny Eagle, Steppe Eagle, and Imperial Eagle soaring above. Other raptors include the African Hawk-Eagle and Verreaux's Eagle. If you keep your eyes peeled, you may also see the Bat Hawk and several types of buzzards like the Common Buzzard and Long-legged Buzzard. As you wander through the grasslands, look out for the large ground birds. The Common Ostrich is a prominent sight, strutting across the savanna. Near the rivers and wetlands, you can find various waterfowl. Keep an eye out for the White-faced Whistling Duck and the Northern Pintail among others. Wading birds are also abundant in the Masai Mara. Plover and lapwing species are often seen near water bodies. You might encounter the Little Ringed Plover and the Kittlitz's Plover. The Blacksmith Lapwing and the Spur-winged Lapwing are also common in these areas. In the wetlands, look for the Greater Painted-snipe and the African Jacana. These birds thrive in the lush environments created by the rivers and marshes. The diversity of birds here reflects the rich ecological variety of the Masai Mara. The different habitats, including riverine forests and acacia woodlands, provide food and nesting sites for many species. This makes the Masai Mara a vital area for bird survival and reproduction. The presence of various raptors indicates a healthy ecosystem with plenty of prey. For birdwatchers, the Masai Mara offers a unique opportunity to see a wide range of African birdlife in one location. Whether you are a seasoned birder or just starting, this region is a must-visit for anyone interested in birds. With its rich diversity and stunning scenery, the Masai Mara truly is a birding hotspot in Kenya.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: After four days of festivities, the World Eskimo Indian Olympics are wrapping up in Fairbanks. This year's event saw world records broken, a crowd a crown passed, and a community gathered to celebrate indigenous culture. Adrian Peterson and Alex Bengal were there today and give us a roundup of the week. The fourth and final day of the 64th annual WEO has arrived. Here at the Carlson Center in Fairbanks, this year's WEO games featured more than 20 competitive events from the four-man carry to the bench reach. Sportsmanship and camaraderie were displayed throughout the games as athletes faced difficult feats. Honestly, I think one foot and two foot are the most challenging if I'm going to be honest. I feel like you know, jumping and then kicking the ball is was a lot for me. Despite the strain and skill testing tasks, newcomers and veteran athletes alike found success during the games with one athlete beating his very own world record on the first day. You just got to have the confidence. Confidence, put the consistency in your practices. Oh, definitely work out a lot and you know, you're you're confident because how are you going to perform if you put in all the work? But the event was about more than sports. It was a chance for the community to get together and for people from around the state and the world to share their culture. Regalia contests with contestants ages 6 months and up showed off unique and elaborate use of hide and cloth. Regalia is really our way to be able to honor our the animals who allowed us to um hunt them. And then also our family, because like I said, it's a family effort. A lot of the patterns are specific to families. Throughout the games, the arena was filled with tables for people to display and sell handmade arts and crafts, made with love and care from all kinds of materials. It's also really healing for your soul, like just sitting there and just healing with your ancestors who were there before you. And a new Miss Wio was crowned Friday night, Jolie Carlson from Bethel and Quetlook. We're still here. We still have our cultures, we still have our traditions, we still have our languages, we know who we are. And it's all still intact and it will be for generations to come. A community gathering to keep culture alive and to pass their knowledge and skills on to the next generation. Adrian Peterson and Alex Bengal, Alaska's News Source.

question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: The London Marathon from pure race to brand playground. Once upon a time, the London Marathon was a straightforward celebration of running. Thousands of runners shared a goal and a spirit for the sport. But fast forward to 2025, it's a whole different marathon. A stage where brands flex their creative muscles as much as the runners do theirs. Take New Balance, for example. They didn't just sponsor the marathon, they created an entire townhouse near Regent Street. Runners could customize their gear, attend motivational talks, and feel like part of an exclusive community. However, not all brand activations hit the mark this year. Nike's never again until next year billboard campaign intended to resonate with runners. Their sentiment post-marathon sparked significant controversy. The phrase never again is deeply associated with the Holocaust remembrance, and its use in this context was seen by many as trivializing a solemn vow. Nike issued an apology, stating that the intent was to motivate runners based on common phrases used in the world of running, but acknowledged the oversight and removed the billboards. This incident underscores the fine lines brands walk when integrating into cultural events. It raises the question, has all this branding overshadowed the essence of the marathon? There's no denying that today's races are as much about social media moments and brand storytelling as they are about the run itself. Every corner turned is another Instagrammable moment. Every mile marker is a brand opportunity, adding to the tapestry of brand engagements. Pure sport, for example, introduced a unique hotel room service. In the days leading up to the marathon, they offered a surprise delivery service to runners staying in London hotels. Participants who signed up via Pure Sports Instagram received recovery kits delivered directly to their rooms. These kits included hydration sachets, magnesium supplements, and marathon socks, essentials designed to aid performance and recovery. Yet, there is a flip side. These brand activations bring fresh eyes to the sport. They attract new runners and allow brands to push creative boundaries. The marathon is no longer just a race. It is a bit of a cultural phenomenon that merges sport, creativity, and community. And in the end, the London Marathon 2025 is a reflection of our times. It's not just about crossing the finish line, but also about the stories told along the way. And perhaps that's not such a bad thing after all. I'd be keen to hear your point of view on this. Do you feel that it is a big brand opportunity to spend some cash and make moves? Or is it for the reasons greater than that? question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Back in the early 2000s, Capcom dropped Metal Walker onto the Game Boy Color and I gotta admit, I thought I had stumbled on some hidden mecha brawler gem. With a name like Metal Walker, you expect something gritty and full of robotic smackdowns, right? Well, you do get robots, but it's more like a Pokemon and a game of pool had a weird random baby. So here's the setup. You play as a kid looking for your dad on an island filled with relics from a mysterious metal called core. As you travel the island, you'll have a companion Metal Walker who's your little battle bot buddy that levels up and evolves based on core units. There are three types, land, marine, and sky. You can switch out orbs to give your bot new abilities. Some will let you smash rocks, one will let you cross water, and each one has different stats to tweak your strategy. Cool in theory, right? Now, the combat is where this game gets totally bonkers. It plays out on a top-down battlefield where instead of picking attacks from a menu, you'll launch your metal walker into enemies billiard style. You'll bounce off walls, collide with opponents, trigger environmental hazards, and hope RNG Jesus is on your side. Each round, a handful of random items spawn on the field, some helpful, some annoying, and by the way, enemies can pick them up too. So it can get chaotic pretty fast. Lining up a good shot is harder than you think, especially with the physics not quite behaving the way you would want it to. Add in the relentless encounter rate and you end up in constant fights that feel more like a chore than a challenge. I found myself wishing I could just turn it down a notch just so I can explore for more than 10 seconds. Speaking of exploration, this isn't a game where you can get lost. The NPCs give clear instructions on how to progress and the descriptions of places are pretty spot on. There's a neat mechanic where you can analyze enemies mid-battle to get new parts, which is probably the closest thing this game has to catching Pokémon. I ended up using a GameFAQs guide because some of the fights were getting too punishing without a bit of extra help. And trust me, the guide made a big difference. There are cheats available if you have a Game Genie or Game Shark. I didn't use any because I really do enjoy leveling up. Visually, Metal Walker is clean for a Game Boy Color title. The sprites are pretty sharp, and it all fits the sci-fi theme. The music was surprisingly great with a large soundtrack you won't get bored with. After all this praise, is it worth it? Honestly, no. The battle system is unique enough to keep me intrigued, but it's not the mecha brawler I expected. So, unless you're a collector or just dying for a fresh take on RPGs, you're better off watching a video or just reading about it.

answer: A video review of the early 2000s Game Boy Color game, "Metal Walker" from Capcom. Set to the game's 8-bit chiptune soundtrack, the reviewer describes a game that plays like "a Pokémon and a game of pool had a weird random baby." They detail the unique combat system where players launch their robot "billiard-style" across a top-down arena, bouncing off walls and into enemies. The review highlights the game's pros, such as its clean sprites and "surprisingly great" music, but heavily criticizes the chaotic, RNG-dependent battles, frustrating physics, and a "relentless encounter rate" that makes the game feel like a chore. The final conclusion is that while the concept is interesting, "Metal Walker" is not worth playing for most, recommending it only to collectors and suggesting others simply watch a video about it instead.

This tutorial provides a step-by-step guide on how to fix Nintendo Switch Joy-Con controllers that are not connecting, pairing, or charging properly. The video outlines a series of troubleshooting methods:

1.  **Power Off the Joy-Cons:** First, disconnect the Joy-Cons from the Switch and press the small circular sync button on the rail of each controller to turn it off. The LED lights should extinguish.

2.  **Update the Switch System:** Go to System Settings on your Switch, scroll down to 'System,' and select 'System Update' to ensure your console's software is current.

3.  **Power Cycle the Switch:** Perform a hard reset by holding down the power button on the console for about 20 seconds, ignoring the on-screen power menu, until the screen turns completely black. Then, power the Switch back on.

4.  **Reconnect and Update Controllers:** Attach the Joy-Cons back to the sides of the Switch. Navigate to System Settings > Controllers and Accessories, and select 'Update Controllers' to install the latest firmware for them.

5.  **Re-sync the Controllers:** If the issue continues, go to the 'Controllers' icon on the home screen, select 'Change Grip/Order,' and then press the sync button on each Joy-Con individually. A green LED light indicates a successful sync. Reattach the controllers to the Switch.

Following these steps should resolve most connection issues with your Joy-Con controllers.

The sharp edges and geometric body panels are not just for show, they also contribute to the vehicle's rigidity and aerodynamics. With its high ground clearance and massive wheels, the Cybertruck still dominates visually on and off the road. Inside the 2026 Cybertruck, you get a minimalist cabin with a large central touchscreen and a yoke style steering wheel. The interior seats six with a fold down front center console and features sustainable materials throughout. The Cybertruck offers multiple power drain options with dual and tri motor setups delivering up to 800 horsepower and over 500 miles of range. It can tow up to 14,000 lbs and accelerate from 0 to 60 in under 2.9 seconds. Pricing starts at around $60,000 and can go beyond 90,000 depending on the configuration. Thanks for watching New Auto Vibe review.

The Eiffel Tower, rising over 300 meters above the city, wasn't always adored. When it was built in 1889, many Parisians despised it. They called it an eyesore, a disgrace to the skyline. But Gustave Eiffel saw the future, and he was right. Today, it's the beating heart of Paris.

But few know what's hidden within. Inside the tower, secret rooms and military bunkers tell stories of war and resistance. Gustave Eiffel had his own private apartment at the top, a sanctuary in the sky, away from the city's chaos.

Now let's descend. Paris is not just beautiful, it's layered. 

Beneath the cobblestone streets lies a second city. Hidden passages, World War II bunkers, secret metro stations, some still in use, others abandoned and lost to time. Urban explorers whisper of the phantom metro lines and government tunnels that link key institutions beneath the surface.

And deeper still, lie the catacombs. Over 6 million souls rest beneath Paris. Skeletons arranged in eerie patterns lining the walls of ancient limestone quarries. This labyrinth stretches for over 200 miles, most of it off-limits, unchartered, and forbidden. 

But the curious always find a way. There are tales of secret cinemas, illegal parties, even entire art galleries hidden in the underworld. Some say there are chambers no one has entered in centuries.

Paris reveals herself only to those who look closely. So next time you stroll by the Seine or gaze at the Eiffel Tower, ask yourself: what lies beneath?

answer: Far away from the noise of the city, in the stillness of the countryside, lives a young woman whose life looks calm from the outside. Her husband works hard, trying to hold their family together, but he cannot understand the storms inside her heart. She walks through the forest, searching for peace, yet the shadows of her mind follow everywhere she goes. The beauty of nature surrounds her, but even in sunlight, she feels trapped in a darker world within herself. This story is not just about love or pain, it is about a woman torn between the desire to live and the weight she carries in her soul. Die My love shows how fragile the human heart can be and how the line between love and despair is sometimes too thin to see.

answer: TikTok's Chinese parent company ByteDance says it has finalized a move to avoid a ban in the US. The deal will create a new majority American-owned joint venture aimed at protecting US user data. It's a major step after years of scrutiny by President Donald Trump, who in 2020 unsuccessfully tried to ban the app over national security concerns. In a post on Thursday, Trump said he is, quote, so happy to have helped in saving TikTok. He also lauded the deal, thanking Chinese President Xi Jinping for, quote, working with us and ultimately approving the deal. The TikTok USDS joint venture will be responsible for securing US data and apps and TikTok's recommendation algorithm. Under the agreement, American and global investors will own 80.1% of the venture, while ByteDance keeps the rest. Tech giant Oracle, private equity group Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX will serve as managing investors, each holding 15%. A White House official says both the US and Chinese governments have approved the deal. The venture will retain and secure TikTok's algorithm using only US data, which will be secured on Oracle's cloud system. Reuters sources said last year that ByteDance would still own TikTok's US operations, but that control of data, content, and algorithms would shift to the new venture.

answer: It was October 17th, 1814, in the St. Giles district of London, a working class area known for narrow streets and dense buildings. The Meux and Company Brewery, a giant operation storing hundreds of thousands of gallons of beer in massive wooden vats. One vat held around 135,000 gallons of porter, strong, dark beer that was a staple of Londoners' diets at the time. Early that morning, disaster struck. One of the enormous wooden vats burst suddenly. The immense pressure caused by fermentation had built up over time. Think of it as a natural soda bottle explosion, but on a massive scale. When the vat broke, it released 135,000 gallons of beer in seconds. But that wasn't all. Another vat, already weakened, collapsed under the force. Soon, a chain reaction sent thousands of gallons gushing through the streets. Wooden beams, barrels, and brewing equipment were swept away in a frothy flood. Eyewitnesses described it as a liquid wall of beer, brown and foaming, smashing fences, walls, and buildings. The flood reportedly reached two-story heights in some places, carving a path of destruction through homes and shops. The flood killed at least eight people, including workers and residents. Most of them were trapped under debris or swept away by the torrent of beer. The brewery faced a huge financial loss, around 23,000 pounds, which was an enormous sum at the time. Surprisingly, insurance didn't cover everything because this type of disaster was considered so unusual. The London beer flood quickly became legendary, inspiring songs, stories, and even jokes about beer as a destructive force. It also highlighted the dangers of industrial scale brewing in cramped urban areas. Today, the event is remembered as a bizarre cautionary tale. Too much beer in the wrong place can be deadly. So next time you lift a pint, remember, in 1814, Londoners didn't just drown in work, poverty or crime, they were almost drowned in beer itself. A historical tsunami fueled entirely by alcohol.

One of those that I think that we'll see AI used a lot more in is areas of diagnostic support. I think what AI is really amazing at is taking a huge amount of context and information and finding key insights, condensing it down, and narrowing down this, you know, potential plethora of conditions that someone may have and finding the key points that will really point to like the root cause diagnosis for an individual. And I think that humans are very good at this too and it's actually very, very difficult to do. But I think that AI has, number one, the ability to ingest stupidly large amounts of context. So while me as a human doctor might need to read a summary of a patient that another doctor has written, it can actually end up, um an AI is able to ingest maybe 20 years of medical context about someone all at once. And so I'm very bullish on AI actually helping with areas such as diagnosis. And I'm actually very bullish on AI getting very strong in this area of diagnosis. That being said, I think there are areas that people thought AI would be amazing in, but haven't seen as much progress as we would have expected. A common one is everyone thought radiologists were going to be out of business. And so radiologists, um, are the people who will look at x-rays, MRIs, and scans and images and make conclusions or diagnosis from those images. answer: From demonstrating its rescue capabilities during disasters to busting a move and serving up drinks. The latest advances in humanoid robot technology are on full display at this year's International Robot Exhibition in Tokyo. The Kaleido 9 is using this toy cat to showcase how it could save people during a disaster. Yoshimoto Matsuda, managing executive officer of Kawasaki Heavy Industries, said the robot is meant to be deployed to disaster areas where access for humans is difficult. We aim to create robots that are robust and reliable for deployment in places where humans cannot work or where they need to work alongside robots. That's why we insist on human-sized robots, so existing equipment like fireproof suits and protective gear can be used without modification. Our vision is not about robots performing repetitive tasks in factories or improving precision, but about working on site, improvising, and using the same tools as humans. Kawasaki spent about a decade developing the robot, which is still in the testing phase. The bot showed off how it can be a lifesaver in other ways, including performing domestic duties like raking up leaves and throwing out the trash. Across the exhibition hall, a dance-off is taking place. This robot was manufactured by Chinese robotics developer Unitree, but programmed and calibrated by Japanese robotics company GMO. Tomohiro Uchida of GMO said the dance moves show just how far robotic development has come. About a year ago, humanoid robots were still very stiff and jerky. People couldn't imagine them functioning in real-world settings. But in the past six months, or even the last three months, the software has been rapidly updated. And now they can perform a variety of movements. So we wanted visitors to see what kind of movements are possible now. As part of that demonstration, we had it perform a dance. It appears to move quite fluidly now. Uchida added that he sees humanoid robots as a solution to help fill gaps in what he called a declining labor force in developed countries.

Welcome to your new ROG Xbox Ally. Getting started couldn't be easier.

When you first boot the device, you'll be greeted with a streamlined Windows setup. After that, you'll be dropped into the new Xbox full-screen experience, which puts your games front and center. But, before you start browsing, you might want to update all of your software. We've already released a number of improvements for day one users. So tap the bell icon in the Xbox app and download any updates it finds. Once that's done, press the command center button on the left side of the device and tap open Armory Crate SE. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: Xiaomi has introduced a new affordable desktop speaker, the Redmi Desktop Speaker 2 Pro. It's currently available on the crowdfunding platform Youpin, and it comes with a four driver configuration. Among the four, there are two passive woofers and two 10-watt race track style speakers. The company says that this driver configuration allows the unit to offer a wide sound stage. Redmi's new desktop speaker 2 Pro also offers a flexible connectivity option. The affordable speaker can play audio from USB, wirelessly through Bluetooth 5.3, and in wired mode through the aux input port. Of course, it's worth noting that the desktop speaker doesn't feature a built-in battery. So, even in the wireless audio mode, it needs to be connected to the wall, and Xiaomi offers a separate adapter for powering the device. Another highlight of this new affordable speaker is the metal grill design, which, paired with the knob on the side, makes the desktop speaker look sleek. There's an integrated RGB light as well, and it can be set in six different effects which can dynamically change with the music. Users also have the option to select one of the 5 EQ presets, depending on what they are listening to. There's a game mode which promises responsive and immersive sound output.

answer: We just got our clearest look yet at DJI's next ultra light drone, and it's not just a refresh. New images from well-known leaker Jasper Ellens via Drone XL reveal design changes, hidden tricks borrowed from DJI's newest models and even the release window. If you thought the mini series had peaked, you might want to sit down for this. The leak front-facing shot instantly gives away a few big upgrades. Front and center, a redesigned gimbal housing a one-inch camera sensor. Between the two main lenses, LAR sensors, an addition that hints at smarter obstacle avoidance. Even the motors have been updated, darker in color, but more importantly, compatible with quick release propellers for faster swaps in the field. Flip it over and the changes keep coming. For the first time in a mini series drone, there's a power lead port, just like the Mavic and Air lines. But the real head turner, it's expected to carry a C0 classification, keeping it under the 249g threshold. That means fewer restrictions in most regions without sacrificing performance. One leak shows ducted propeller guards with low noise tips, a design that echoes the DJI flip. The difference? These guards are removable, giving pilots the flexibility to fly light or add protection depending on the environment. This is where the Mini 5 Pro might completely change how people use a travel drone. Leaks suggest a side mounted quick launch button that can send the drone airborne and start recording. No controller required. If that sounds familiar, it's because DJI has already experimented with it on the Neo and the flip, but this will be the first time it lands on a Mini Pro. According to Jasper Ellens, the Fly More Combo with the RC2 controller will land around $1,200. And while DJI hasn't officially confirmed it, insiders are pointing to a September release window. If these leaks hold true, the Mini 5 Pro could be DJI's most versatile sub 250G drone yet, bridging the gap between portability and pro-level shooting. I'll be covering every update as it drops. question: Transcribe the speech content and output the transcription.
answer: At the NATO Summit held in The Hague on June 25th, 2025, leaders from the 32-member alliance pledged a significant increase in defense spending and reaffirmed their commitment to mutual protection under Article 5 of the NATO treaty. The summit was brief and carefully orchestrated to accommodate US President Donald Trump. NATO leaders endorsed a new target of allocating 5% of GDP to defense spending by 2035, a sharp rise from the previous 2% goal. This decision addresses both Trump's demands and concerns over increasing threats from Russia following its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The official statement reaffirmed NATO's ironclad commitment to Article 5, declaring that an attack on one member is an attack on all. Trump had previously caused alarm by saying there were numerous definitions of the clause, but at the summit, he reassured allies, stating, we're with them all the way. The new spending breakdown includes 3.5% of GDP for core defense, such as troops and weapons, and 1.5% for broader security needs like cybersecurity, infrastructure resilience, and protection of pipelines. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte acknowledged the financial challenge for European nations and Canada but emphasized its necessity, citing the current international security climate. Rutte, the former Dutch Prime Minister, noted full backing from NATO members, though Spain insisted it could meet its obligations without hitting the 5% mark, a stance Rutte diplomatically accepted to keep the summit smooth. President Trump praised the deal, calling it a great victory for everybody, and highlighting that nations were finally aligning with his long-standing call for increased contributions. The summit was choreographed to maintain harmony, including shortening official proceedings and hosting Trump at the Royal Palace. Trump described the hosts, King Willem Alexander and Queen Maxima, as beautiful and spectacular and posted positively about the event on Truth Social. Belgium's Prime Minister Bart De Wever labeled the spending hike as historic, urging Europe to take greater responsibility for its security. Trump also met briefly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, referring to him as a nice guy and claimed ongoing discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. However, NATO will steer clear of Kiev's membership bid for now, as Trump has rejected it. Despite differences, NATO leaders emphasized unity, with Rutte affirming that US commitment to Article 5 remains firm and unwavering.

See, we all want Samsung to bring fresh new design to the Galaxy S and Galaxy Z series every year, but honestly, it's not easy to change the classic smartphone shape that much anymore. Thanks to trusted leaker on leaks, we now have detailed images and a 360 degree video of the Galaxy S25 FE. And looking at them, the phone will keep its 6.7 inches Super AMOLED screen with a smooth 120 Hz refresh rate. Some rumor says the screen might get really bright up to 2600 nits, but that's not confirmed yet. The Galaxy S25 FE will be a bit thicker than the Galaxy S25, but still thinner than the last year's Galaxy S24 FE. Now, looking at the pictures, it seems Samsung has made screen bezels thinner on this model. We don't know if the price will go up, but if it does, it might be around $50 more at launch. Inside, there is some confusion about the processor. The Galaxy S25 FE could come with either Samsung's own Exynos 2400 chip or a MediaTek Diamond City 9400. If Samsung uses the MediaTek chip, it might really excite fans and shake up the market. Moving on, the front camera will be a big upgrade, a 12 megapixel sensor just like the other Galaxy S25 models, improving on the previous 10 megapixel camera from the older FE. The back cameras probably won't change much. One thing we do know is the Galaxy S25 FE will run one UI 8 right out of the box. Plus, Samsung promises seven years of software updates. They started testing the one UI 8 software for this phone last month and have expanded testing to more regions recently. Some insiders also think the Galaxy S25 FE might offer up to 12 gigs of RAM and 256 gigs of storage even in the base version. So, if the price in the US is around $700 compared to a $650 for last year's model with less RAM and storage, the new FE could be a great deal. So, overall, the Galaxy S25 FE is shaping up to be a solid upgrade with a sleek design, brighter display, better selfie camera, and more powerful specs. If Samsung really does launch it with a 12 gigs of RAM and a fair price, this could be one of the best value flagship of the year. So, what do you guys think of this Galaxy S25 FE? Let me know in the comments. With that being said, subscribe if you like, and I will see you in the next one.

The narration captures the mounting tension, the key moments, and the sheer belief that powered the team to an incredible 4-0 victory, securing a 4-3 aggregate win.

Some matches are remembered for goals. Some, for glory. But once in a lifetime, there comes a game that changes everything. This is the story of one of football's most unbelievable comebacks.

May 1st, 2019. Camp Nou. Barcelona 3, 0 Liverpool. The Catalan giants, with Messi leading the way, had all but booked their place in the Champions League final. Liverpool, without Salah and Firmino for the second leg, were broken, injured, and written off.

The mission at Anfield: score four, concede none. Anfield wasn't just hosting a game; it was preparing for a miracle. Jürgen Klopp told his players, "If we fail, let's fail in the most beautiful way."

Minute 7: Henderson drives forward, shoots. Ter Stegen parries. Origi taps it in. One. Belief starts to flicker.

But they still need one more. Minute 79: Corner to Liverpool. Ball boy throws it fast. Trent Alexander-Arnold sees a sleeping defense. One of the sharpest minds in football does the unthinkable. Corner taken quickly! Origi! 4-0!

The final whistle blows. Liverpool 4, Barcelona 0. Aggregate 4-3. Against all odds, the Reds had done it. Not just a win, a statement to the world.

This wasn't just football. It was belief. Passion. Anfield at its loudest, its boldest, its most beautiful. In 90 minutes, Liverpool didn't just beat Barcelona; they made history.

answer: On the 17th of October 1814, a strange and destructive event took place at the Moe and Co. S Horseshoe brewery, located at the junction of Tottenham Court Road and Oxford Street in London, England. The brewery contained several enormous wooden vats, some of them 22 feet tall, filled with porter, a dark London beer that was extremely popular during that period. On that day, the hoop of one of the huge vats suddenly broke, causing the vat to burst and release its contents. The force of the escaping beer ruptured the stopcock of a second large vat, which also began to discharge. Several other vats were damaged in the chain reaction. In total, between 580,000 and 1,470,000 liters of porter flooded out, smashing through the brewery's rear wall, which was 25 ft high. Behind the brewery stood the St. Giles's rookery, one of London's poorest and most crowded slum districts. Once the wall collapsed, a wave of porter about 15 ft high swept into New Street and Great Russell Street, destroying homes and flooding basements. Everyone inside the brewery survived, but according to the coroner's report, eight people in the surrounding neighborhood were killed either by drowning, injuries from collapsing walls, or being trapped in flooded rooms. Eyewitnesses described the area afterwards as looking like the aftermath of an earthquake. Rumors later spread of people collecting the spilled beer, widespread drunkenness, and even deaths from alcohol poisoning in the following days. However, these stories appear exaggerated. The corner ruled that the disaster was an act of God, meaning the brewery was not held legally responsible and paid no compensation. The incident contributed to the decline of large wooden fermentation vats, which were eventually phased out across the brewing industry. The horseshoe brewery was later demolished.
